rated_messages.input_message: If leaving social situations to avoid smokers feels awkward, make sure you have something to do instead - take sugar free mints, lollipops or low fat snacks to chew, or use a stress ball.
Pause. Notice what triggered you to smoke in the past. Now take one deep breath and remind yourself that you do not need to smoke.

Don't let anyone tell you how you should or shouldn't feel today. You feel how you feel and that's it. If you're happy and grateful then enjoy the moment, if you're angry and frustrated, know that this will pass.
Instead of smoking, take 10 deep, slow breaths and count them. Pay attention to what your breathing feels like. If you lose count, that's okay, just start over at 1 until you get to 10.
Ask yourself, "From 0-10, how willing am I to let this urge pass without smoking?" Let it pass to be closer to the things that matter most to you.
Setting small goals when you feel unmotivated is best. Maybe a small goal for now is to breathe deeply for the next 3 minutes instead of smoking.

Think about what is really important to you. Maybe it's spending time with family or a friend, exercising, doing something spiritual, or creating something. Whatever it is, take a step in that direction.
Whenever you think about smoking, listen to your favorite song and sing it out loud!
Don't test yourself needlessly. If this social situation gets uncomfortable then leave briefly if you can. It really helps and it's fine to do it more than once!
When your mind tells you that you will be less stressed after smoking a cigarette, remember that you don't have to listen to that thought. It's just a thought and nothing more.
